gaps: The plan's sector-level end-of-plan (2028) targets are in a separate Results Matrix (RM) 2023-2028 that BPDA has not published; only the macroeconomic table has 2028 targets in the plan itself. Sector targets above are the 2023-2025 annual targets that the Bangsamoro Development Report 2024 reprints from the RM.
No BDR 2025 found; the Midterm Update (Aug 2026) reports most sector actuals only to 2024.

Actuals with no published target: basic and functional literacy (FLEMMS 2024), household electrification, basic sanitation, index crime volume, SGLG awards, poverty incidence among population (also no 2025 BARMM figure found), displaced families (MSSD: 243,157 families displaced in 2025, Midterm p.220).

Targets with no usable actual: GRDP per capita, industry and services growth for 2025 (PSA 2025 regional release not retrievable); annual average inflation for 2025; gross capital formation (dropped: BDR 2024 gives 8.1% for 2024 while the Midterm Update gives 21.4%); poverty gap and severity ('downward trend', no figures).

Health outcome targets that would matter most to residents (facility-based births, skilled birth attendance, modern contraceptive use) are not in the published RM rows; NDHS 2022 values were not collected.
Mortality and stunting in the plan's own tracker come from MOH facility reporting, not surveys; a survey-based 2028 target for these was not found.
Free public Wi-Fi: the plan’s 2025 target is 15 sites, but its 2024 progress report prints the 2024 result as “37% (Intranet)”, a different measure, so it is not scored.
doubts: PSA websites (psa.gov.ph, rssobarmm.psa.gov.ph, openstat) block automated fetches (Cloudflare 403). PSA figures came from the PSA FLEMMS PDF hosted by ABS-CBN, Bangsamoro Information Office articles quoting PSA releases, and search-engine extracts of the PSA BARMM LFS release (https://rssobarmm.psa.gov.ph/content/number-unemployed-barmm-increased-93-thousand-bangsamoros-aged-15-years-and-over-2025). Each should be checked against the PSA page in a browser.

2025 LFS figures (unemployment 3.9%, underemployment 12.6%, LFPR 73.5%) came from a search extract of the PSA BARMM page; the same extract lists Sulu among provinces, so the 2025 labour series may still include Sulu while GRDP 2025 and poverty 2025 exclude it.

Poverty 2023 appears as 23.5% (PSA Aug 2024, with Sulu) and 26% (PSA Aug 2026, apparently without Sulu). The BIO article does not say why it changed: https://bangsamoro.gov.ph/news/latest-news/barmm-posts-biggest-drop-in-family-poverty-incidence-nationwide-psa-says/

GRDP: PSA restated 2024 growth from 2.7% to 3.4% when it moved Sulu to Region IX (https://bangsamoro.gov.ph/news/latest-news/barmm-economy-grows-5-in-2025-ranks-6th-fastest-in-ph/). The 2.7% in BDR 2024 and the Midterm Update is the old with-Sulu number.
BDR 2024 and the Midterm Update disagree on several 2024 values: services growth (5.1 vs 6.1), inflation (3.7 vs 3.9), GCF share (8.1 vs 21.4), elementary net enrolment (63.84 vs 66.89).
Midterm Update Table 4.1 and its own text give different revised targets for GRDP per capita (10-12 vs 8.0-12.0) and AFF growth (10-12 vs 6.0-8.0).

Health rows in BDR 2024 Table 16 carry % signs on per-1,000 and per-100,000 rates, baselines below the targets (IMR 2.21 vs 4.5 target; U5MR 2.34 vs 7.5) and a 2025 immunisation target of '10%'; these are reproduced as printed.

Stunting: the BDR 2024 RM reports 21% (2023) and 7.1% (2024) from MOH data; the Midterm Update cites 34.3% (ENNS 2023) and also, confusingly, says the region's level is 'lower than the national prevalence'. The FNRI report (https://enutrition.fnri.dost.gov.ph/images/nns-2023/3.%20Preschool.pdf) returned an error, so 34.3% was not checked at source.
Basic literacy 2024: PSA final 81.0% vs Midterm Update 84.2% (possibly the preliminary figure).
The original 2023 plan PDF has its prose rasterised (text appears only in tables); prose targets were checked by OCR of all 424 pages and none beyond the macro table were found.
